newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 10.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Apple Computer ousted Chairman and CEO Gilbert Amelio.
* Wells Fargo warned that quarterly earnings will come in nearly one-third below analysts estimates.
* McDonald's Corp announced a new team to revitalize its U.S. business.
* President Clinton will insist on changes to the proposed tobacco pact.
* Microsoft is again revamping its strategy for the Microsoft Network.
* A group led by BellSouth won a wireless license in Sao Paulo, paying $2.5 billion.
* The treasury received a tepid reception for its first auction of inflation-protected securities with five-year maturities.
* Music sales continued to show strong growth in the first half.
* A court found that companies can write off the costs of hostile takeover defenses as ordinary business expenses.
* Anadarko Petroleum made an oil discovery in the Sahara Desert that could mean one of Algeria's top fields is larger than had been thought.
* Detroit Diesel agreed to buy Outboard Marine for $320 million in cash and stock, plus assumed debt.
* Equitable named Edward Miller president and chief executive.
* Treasury prices rose Wednesday, helped by investor optimism that inflation would not accelerate anytime soon.
* Shares of several companies started by Wayne Huizenga have fallen sharply in recent months, despite a boyant stock market.
